rapa-nui-decline.summary: Once told as a parable of a society destroying its own environment, the island's collapse is now widely attributed to introduced rats and, decisively, to contact.
rapa-nui-decline.note: The popular account of self-inflicted ecological collapse is heavily disputed. Recent work points instead to rats eating palm seeds, and above all to European contact — disease and the Peruvian slave raids of the 1860s, which reduced the population to barely a hundred people.

edo-period.summary: Two and a half centuries of Tokugawa peace under near-total isolation, during which Japan urbanised heavily and developed a distinctive popular culture of woodblock prints and theatre.

adi-granth-compiled.summary: Guru Arjan compiled the hymns of the first five Gurus, together with verses by Kabir, Ravidas, Namdev and Sufi poets — sixty-five years after Guru Nanak's death, and unusually for scripture, largely in the authors' own words rather than reported.

texts.title: Sikh texts at the Internet Sacred Text Archive

telescope.summary: A Dutch lens-grinder's device that, pointed upward the following year, ended the idea of a perfect and unchanging heaven.
telescope.significance: Pointed at the sky in 1609, it ended the idea of a perfect and unchanging heaven within a single lifetime.
telescope.note: From the Dutch lens-grinders to the instrument being standard equipment in astronomy.

locke.summary: Held that the mind begins without innate ideas and that government is legitimate only by consent of the governed.

spinoza.summary: Identified God with nature itself and argued for freedom of thought, for which he was expelled from his community and read in secret.

taj-mahal.summary: Mausoleum built by Shah Jahan for Mumtaz Mahal at Agra, the high point of Mughal architecture.

qing-dynasty.summary: China's last dynasty, Manchu in origin, which tripled the empire's territory and then spent its final century losing wars, territory and legitimacy to industrial powers.

newton.summary: Showed that the same law of gravitation governs a falling apple and an orbiting moon, and built the calculus needed to prove it.
newton.significance: He showed that the same law governs a falling apple and an orbiting moon - the first demonstration that the heavens run on rules discoverable from the ground.
newton.note: Born 25 December 1642 by the Julian calendar England still used; 4 January 1643 in the Gregorian calendar used here.

great-plague-london.summary: Killed roughly a quarter of London's population in eighteen months, and was followed the next year by the fire that burned much of the city.
